The frozen filter registry ensures temporal consistency by constraining data windows and enforcing minimum sample sizes. The family disagreement index measures inconsistency in sample sizes across competing models. These primitives form a dual system: one for validating forecasts against benchmarks (CRPS), another for ensuring internal coherence (frozen filter), and a third for detecting model divergence (family disagreement). Failure modes include insufficient data (min_prior violation), inconsistent sampling (family disagreement), and incorrect benchmarking (CRPS misalignment).
